html:
The Garrwa, also written Garawa, are an Aboriginal Australian people of the Gulf of Carpentaria coast and hinterland, east of Borroloola along the Northern Territory and Queensland border.

Their language and that of the Waanyi make up the small Garrwan family, not related to the large Pama-Nyungan family. Other neighbours were the Yanyuwa on the coast and islands, the Ganggalida to the east and the Binbinga to the west.

Cattle stations and the droving route through the Gulf brought violent clashes from the 1880s. Many Garrwa people live today at Borroloola and at Robinson River.
sum: The Garrwa, also written Garawa, are an Aboriginal Australian people of the Gulf of Carpentaria coast and hinterland, east of Borroloola along the Northern Territory and Queensland border.
